newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count up 13 to 961 in week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count up 13 to 961 in week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 961 as of May 30, up 13 from the prior week and 196 above the year-ago total of 765, Baker Hughes Inc. said Friday.
The number of rigs drilling on land rose by 13 to 816, while rigs working offshore were down one at 119. The number of rigs active in inland waters rose by one to 26.
Among the individual states, the biggest changes occurred in Texas, which was up by six. Louisiana was up by three and Wyoming was up by two.
The Gulf of Mexico rig count dipped one to 114.

A total of 395 rigs were exploring for crude oil, up eight from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas rose by five to 562, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects remained at four.
There were 197 rigs drilling directionally, 76 drilling horizontally and 688 drilling vertically.
In Canada, the number of working rigs fell by 23 to 257, vs. 204 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
Separately, Offshore Data Services said there were 170 rigs under contract in the Gulf of Mexico off Texas and Louisiana as of May 30, unchanged from the period ending May 23.
The utilization rate for rigs working in the Gulf, based on a total fleet of 179, was unchanged at 95.0 percent.
The number of working rigs in the European/Mediterranean area was unchanged at 106 rigs under contract out of a total fleet of 107, an unchanged utilization rate of 99.1 percent.
The worldwide rig count was up one at 578 out of a total fleet of 605, with a utilization rate up from 95.4 percent at 95.5 percent.
